recent_commits.body: repro_docker_available() tries again when Docker answers late (#560)
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: repro_docker_available() tries again when Docker answers late (#560)
recent_commits.body:
A docker info that took more than 15 seconds was reported as Docker not
running, which stopped the paper. A late answer now gets two more tries, of
30 and 60 seconds. If all three are late, the message says Docker did not
answer. An error answer still reports at once that Docker is not running.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Reuse saved archive files (#561); make saved file names safe on every system (#557)
recent_commits.body:
Files inside an archive that were already saved are now found by their
size and reused, so they are not fetched or unpacked again on every run.

Names that are not valid on some operating system (a colon, * ? " < > |,
control characters, a final dot or space, reserved names) are now changed
in the same way on every system, wherever metacheck saves a file. A script
that cannot be written no longer stops reproducibility_check for the paper.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: data_check reads every sheet of a spreadsheet that holds a table (#555)
recent_commits.body: Each table of a file with several has its columns under source_file = "file.xlsx [sheet]", and a new column sheet names the sheet; a file with one table keeps its own name. Sheets of notes and codebooks are documentation when the file has another table. FAIR_repo() names each variable's CSV by its sheet, writes a CSV per sheet of an .ods file, and writes dataset_description.json also when the first sheet's CSV went to documentation/.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() works on a temporary copy and keeps recovered code; data_check is faster on large files (#554); code_check no longer writes into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() runs its checks on a temporary copy, so the folder is only read. It keeps code recovered from output files as scripts, changes the paths scripts write to, replaces setwd() only for a written-out folder, no folder or the script's own folder, changes links in the folder's README to the files' new places, names each variable's file as it is in the copy, and has an execute argument for the library() calls reproducibility_check adds.

data_check's column checks work on each distinct value once and skip text work for plain number columns; 498 columns compared gave identical results. codebook_check no longer converts columns without documented codes. Pages made by pkgdown are not taken for rendered analyses.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() keeps folders, the authors' README and results apart; requirements.txt lists only installable Python packages; output readers keep backslashes
recent_commits.body:
From converting 20 real repositories:
- psychds_file_plan() keeps a file's folders inside data/, materials/ and
  documentation/ as well as analysis/, ignores a top folder that holds
  every file (GitHub downloads), and drops a first folder that only names
  the kind of file. Data in one folder per condition lost which condition
  it was, and the authors' README was moved out of the top.
- FAIR_repo() puts a file a script writes and no script reads, and a
  fitted model, in outputs/, and points scripts there; converts an R data
  file only when it holds a table and no CSV of that name is next to it;
  writes requirements.txt with Python packages only, without the standard
  library and under their pip names; takes the title from the folder's own
  README; marks missing authors "unknown"; shows variable tables only when
  there are labels; writes no dataset_description.json without data.
- The R, Mplus and Stata output readers pad lines in characters instead of
  with formatC(), which dropped a backslash and split columns wrongly.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Scripts keep their folders inside analysis/
recent_commits.body:
psychds_file_plan() put every script flat in analysis/, so two scripts
with one name collided and code that finds its own modules by folder
stopped working. A script now keeps its folders below the folder all
scripts of its study share.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() converts a local folder and never goes online; identical files are left out; READMEs in subfolders keep their folder; archives of your own are not unpacked into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo(path, output_dir, paper) now converts a folder on the
researcher's own computer, running the checks as report_repository()
does, with local_only for every check. Nothing is downloaded, no link is
followed, and the folder is not changed. The paper is optional and gives
the title, authors, CRediT roles and funding. Online sources, result
reuse and the download arguments are removed.

A file from an archive that is identical to a file next to it, and a
README identical to another, are left out and listed in CHANGES.md. A data
file that holds no table is kept as it is instead of reported as failed,
and two different originals with one name no longer overwrite each other.
Paths of the folder are removed from the saved check results.

psychds_file_plan() puts a README in a subfolder in documentation/, named
after its folder; every README went to the top and they replaced each
other. .archive_dest() unpacks next to itself only an archive metacheck
downloaded; any archive in the temporary folder counted, so an uploaded
folder got a "<zip>.contents" folder written into it.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() writes a reorganised, documented copy of a paper's repository; reproducibility_check copies same-named files from their own place and changes only quoted paths
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() places every file where the Psych-DS layout puts it, writes
non-CSV data as CSV next to the original, changes the paths and setwd()
lines of R and Python scripts, and writes dataset_description.json,
ro-crate-metadata.json, a README (only where the repository has none),
requirements.txt, CHANGES.md and logs/. It reuses the checks in a captured
result and runs only the missing ones.

reproducibility_check looked up a file's copy by name and took the first,
so same-named files from different folders got one file's content, and it
replaced a path wherever its text appeared, so x.csv also changed
"old_x.csv".
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: API keys work the same way for every repository, and visitors can use their own when the server's run out
recent_commits.body:
- R/api-keys.R: each key is read from an option first and an environment
  variable second, checked once per R session, and left out with a warning
  when the service refuses it. A refused key or a reached limit is recorded in
  a state folder all R sessions share (METACHECK_STATE_DIR), and
  api_key_status() gives the message for the visitor. api_keys_use() sets a
  visitor's own keys for one job. New github_pat() and openalex_key().
- GitHub, GitLab, OSF, Dataverse, Dryad, ResearchBox and OpenAlex use this;
  keys go only to their own host; a GitHub or GitLab limit now reports the
  repository as not listed instead of empty; ResearchBox's count of "unfound"
  answers moved to the state folder, where it is no longer lost after each job.
- osf_app(): a wrong typed token no longer clears OSF_PAT.
- The three apps: a folded box "Your own API keys (optional)" and a notice
  when a key of the server was refused or used up; the keys go to the
  visitor's own job only. The plumber API takes key_<service> fields.
- Tests: setup.R's resets now run when all tests have run (teardown_env());
  before, they ran at once, so tests wrote to the package source and the
  user's own state folder. test-app-repocheck.R puts metacheck.repo_cache.dir
  back after the app's job.

  web page stays the fallback

_new_commits.message: repro_docker_available() tries again when Docker answers late (#560)

running, which stopped the paper. A late answer now gets two more tries, of
30 and 60 seconds. If all three are late, the message says Docker did not
answer. An error answer still reports at once that Docker is not running.

_new_commits.message: Reuse saved archive files (#561); make saved file names safe on every system (#557)
_new_commits.body:
Files inside an archive that were already saved are now found by their
size and reused, so they are not fetched or unpacked again on every run.

Names that are not valid on some operating system (a colon, * ? " < > |,
control characters, a final dot or space, reserved names) are now changed
in the same way on every system, wherever metacheck saves a file. A script
that cannot be written no longer stops reproducibility_check for the paper.
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: Merge pull request #556 from scienceverse/convert_repo_FAIR
_new_commits.body: FAIR_repo() converts a local folder into a FAIR copy; data_check reads every sheet and is faster (0.4.2.1)
_new_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

_new_commits.message: NEWS: fix the 0.4.1 heading
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: Version 0.4.2.1
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: data_check reads every sheet of a spreadsheet that holds a table (#555)
_new_commits.body: Each table of a file with several has its columns under source_file = "file.xlsx [sheet]", and a new column sheet names the sheet; a file with one table keeps its own name. Sheets of notes and codebooks are documentation when the file has another table. FAIR_repo() names each variable's CSV by its sheet, writes a CSV per sheet of an .ods file, and writes dataset_description.json also when the first sheet's CSV went to documentation/.
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: FAIR_repo() works on a temporary copy and keeps recovered code; data_check is faster on large files (#554); code_check no longer writes into your folder
_new_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() runs its checks on a temporary copy, so the folder is only read. It keeps code recovered from output files as scripts, changes the paths scripts write to, replaces setwd() only for a written-out folder, no folder or the script's own folder, changes links in the folder's README to the files' new places, names each variable's file as it is in the copy, and has an execute argument for the library() calls reproducibility_check adds.

data_check's column checks work on each distinct value once and skip text work for plain number columns; 498 columns compared gave identical results. codebook_check no longer converts columns without documented codes. Pages made by pkgdown are not taken for rendered analyses.
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: FAIR_repo() keeps folders, the authors' README and results apart; requirements.txt lists only installable Python packages; output readers keep backslashes
_new_commits.body:
From converting 20 real repositories:
- psychds_file_plan() keeps a file's folders inside data/, materials/ and
  documentation/ as well as analysis/, ignores a top folder that holds
  every file (GitHub downloads), and drops a first folder that only names
  the kind of file. Data in one folder per condition lost which condition
  it was, and the authors' README was moved out of the top.
- FAIR_repo() puts a file a script writes and no script reads, and a
  fitted model, in outputs/, and points scripts there; converts an R data
  file only when it holds a table and no CSV of that name is next to it;
  writes requirements.txt with Python packages only, without the standard
  library and under their pip names; takes the title from the folder's own
  README; marks missing authors "unknown"; shows variable tables only when
  there are labels; writes no dataset_description.json without data.
- The R, Mplus and Stata output readers pad lines in characters instead of
  with formatC(), which dropped a backslash and split columns wrongly.
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: Scripts keep their folders inside analysis/
_new_commits.body:
psychds_file_plan() put every script flat in analysis/, so two scripts
with one name collided and code that finds its own modules by folder
stopped working. A script now keeps its folders below the folder all
scripts of its study share.
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: FAIR_repo() converts a local folder and never goes online; identical files are left out; READMEs in subfolders keep their folder; archives of your own are not unpacked into your folder
_new_commits.body:
FAIR_repo(path, output_dir, paper) now converts a folder on the
researcher's own computer, running the checks as report_repository()
does, with local_only for every check. Nothing is downloaded, no link is
followed, and the folder is not changed. The paper is optional and gives
the title, authors, CRediT roles and funding. Online sources, result
reuse and the download arguments are removed.

A file from an archive that is identical to a file next to it, and a
README identical to another, are left out and listed in CHANGES.md. A data
file that holds no table is kept as it is instead of reported as failed,
and two different originals with one name no longer overwrite each other.
Paths of the folder are removed from the saved check results.

psychds_file_plan() puts a README in a subfolder in documentation/, named
after its folder; every README went to the top and they replaced each
other. .archive_dest() unpacks next to itself only an archive metacheck
downloaded; any archive in the temporary folder counted, so an uploaded
folder got a "<zip>.contents" folder written into it.
_new_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.message: FAIR_repo() writes a reorganised, documented copy of a paper's repository; reproducibility_check copies same-named files from their own place and changes only quoted paths
_new_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() places every file where the Psych-DS layout puts it, writes
non-CSV data as CSV next to the original, changes the paths and setwd()
lines of R and Python scripts, and writes dataset_description.json,
ro-crate-metadata.json, a README (only where the repository has none),
requirements.txt, CHANGES.md and logs/. It reuses the checks in a captured
result and runs only the missing ones.

reproducibility_check looked up a file's copy by name and took the first,
so same-named files from different folders got one file's content, and it
replaced a path wherever its text appeared, so x.csv also changed
"old_x.csv".
_new_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Check only single-value defaults for length in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 required every setting to be length 1, so a mapper made from a
`.fn` with a setting such as `bounds = NULL` or `scale = c(1, 7)` failed on
every call, even at its default. Only settings whose default is a single
value are checked now; enums count, since their default resolves to one
string.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Expect the length error for length-2 settings in two stale tests
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 checks every setting's length before its value, so
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` and `percent = c(TRUE, FALSE)` now fail with
"must be length 1, not 2". Two expectations still had the old wording.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the digits_* columns as integers in all mapper tiers
recent_commits.body:
* `n` was already integer when lossless, but `digits_x` and `digits_sd` were
double although they are always whole numbers. `function_map()` and
`function_map_seq()` now pass them through `as_integer_if_lossless()`; the
total-n tier inherits the basic mapper's columns.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut NEWS items that describe changes since 0.6.1 only within the branch
recent_commits.body:
* Each item was checked against scrutiny 0.6.1, installed from main. Dropped:
the integer `digits_*` columns, the `items = 2` partial match, the error for
two key arguments naming one column, the `grim_binomial()` and
`grim_plot_rates()` clause, GRIMMER running indefinitely, the integer
`diff_var`, `1e-300` having 315 decimal places, and mappers failing under
`lapply()`.
* Reworded items that 0.6.1 handled differently from the stated earlier
state: a seq mapper with nothing to disperse already warned, and a total-n
case without group pairs failed rather than vanishing.
* `grim_map(percent = TRUE)` now says that `x` stays a percentage, which is
the actual change from 0.6.1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require every setting to be length 1 in the mappers
recent_commits.body:
* The mappers checked the settings with `check_lengths_congruent()`,
which allowed one of them to be longer than 1. An enum such as
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` then reached `rlang::arg_match()`,
whose error says it is 'not "se"', though "se" is valid; `percent =
c(TRUE, FALSE)` reached the test. The vectorized functions had their
own length-1 check with a better message.

* `check_setting_length()` is that check, shared by `map_value_sets()`,
`function_map()`, and the total-n factory, which reads an enum before
`fn()` does. In the mappers it runs after `check_rounding_args()`, which
keeps its own message for the rounding arguments.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` had no caller left and is deleted with its
tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare x to a power of 10 in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `abs(x) >= 10^(15 - digits)` is the same condition as the one on
`floor(log10(abs(x)))`, but exact for every power of ten, so it needs
no correction for `log10()` rounding up just below one. The count in
the message comes from the integer part written out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show the reported values in full in the size error
recent_commits.body:
* `check_values_size()` formatted the value set with `format()`'s
default 7 significant digits, so a reported `x = 0.123456789` was
named as `x = 0.1234568`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name items_averaged in the size error of the values functions
recent_commits.body:
* Two value sets that differ only in `items_averaged` read the same in
the message otherwise.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave one or two missing strings undecided in is_seq_linear()
recent_commits.body:
* A logical or numeric `NA` is some number, and any two numbers are
linear, but a missing string could be no number at all, so
`is_seq_linear(c(NA_character_, NA_character_))` is `NA` again.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check an enum in the total-n mappers before n_min_fn() reads it
recent_commits.body:
* `n_min_fn()` ran on the raw settings, so a two-value or `NULL`
`sd_meaning` failed in `sd_min_n()` with a plain R error instead of
the mapper's own. Each enum given is now validated with
`arg_match_in_export()` right after `resolve_enums()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count the integer digits of x exactly in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `floor(log10(abs(x)))` rounds up to the next whole number just below a
power of 10, so 999999999999999 and 99999.9999999999 were rejected as
having 16 significant digits. The exponent is now corrected downward
when `10^exponent` exceeds `abs(x)`, as in `next_square_root()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a value with more than 15 significant digits
recent_commits.body:
* check_newly_numeric() capped digits_x at 15 but not the integer
digits of x, so 33.33333333333333 with digits_x = 14 passed although a
double does not hold 16 significant digits and the tests are not exact
there. The sum of the two is now capped at 15.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return TRUE for two values with an infinity among them
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(c(1, Inf)) was FALSE: the step Inf - 1 is Inf, which
dplyr::near() cannot compare to itself. Any two values are linear, so
the step check only runs for three or more.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve a NULL n_min to the default in every total-n mapper
recent_commits.body:
* Only the function-valued .n_min branch replaced a NULL, so
grim_map_total_n(n_min = NULL) passed it on to disperse_total(), which
dispersed down to a group of 0.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Report a missing required argument on a 0-row data frame, too
recent_commits.body:
* A mapper tests its first row on its own so that a missing digits_x or
items_averaged is reported by the test function. With no row to test,
the check was skipped and the mapper returned an empty tibble. It now
tests a row of missing values if a required argument is missing.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve an enum given as its whole set in every tier
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_total_n(sd_meaning = SD_MEANINGS) failed in sd_min_n(),
since the total-n factory reads the settings for n_min before fn()
runs, from the values as given. grimmer(sd_meaning = SD_MEANINGS)
failed the length check for the same reason, while grimmer_map()
accepted the set.

* The resolution to the first string, as rlang::arg_match() would do
it, is one helper now, resolve_enums(), with eval_enum_defaults() for
the sets, used by function_map(), function_map_total_n(), and
map_value_sets().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return TRUE for a linear sequence that no missing value could break
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(NA) and is_seq_linear(c(NA, NA)) were NA, although any
one or two values are linear, so the missing values could not change
the answer. NA is only for a question that they could decide either
way, as the too-short case returning FALSE already assumed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give a seq mapper's zero-row output the columns of its usual output
recent_commits.body:
* With no case to disperse from, the fallback kept every column of the
basic mapper's output, while the re-tests drop the columns of data that
play no role in the test. The fallback now keeps what is left of the
key result column plus the columns fn() added.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return FALSE for an all-NA vector too short for the sequence
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_ascending(NA) was NA while is_seq_ascending(5) was FALSE: the
all-NA rule ran before the length check, although no values could make
a single one ascending. The length check comes first now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let the total-n mappers' n_min follow sd_meaning
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_total_n() and debit_map_total_n() had n_min = 2 whatever
the sd_meaning, so under "sd_pop" or "sd_sample_or_pop", where a group
of 1 has an SD, such pairs were silently left out. The seq tier already
adapted its out_min through sd_min_n().

* function_map_total_n() takes a function of the settings as .n_min, as
function_map_seq() does for .var_bounds. The manufactured function's
n_min then defaults to NULL, which the body resolves, and the resolved
value is what the recorded setting counts as the default.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Document that "ties_even" shares the bounds of "even"
recent_commits.body:
* roundwork gives both methods inclusive bounds on both sides, since
base::round() decides a tie on the binary double, so grim(5.3, 4, 1, 1,
rounding = "ties_even") is TRUE although 21 / 4 rounds to 5.2 in
decimal. The docs mentioned the exception for "even" only.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep grim_explain()'s example means apart from the bounds of x
recent_commits.body:
* divide() formatted a sum divided by n without the bounds to avoid, so
with n above 10^digits_x the shown mean landed on a stated bound:
499 / 999 printed as 0.4995, the bound it falls short of, and the text
contradicted itself. It passes the bounds now, as debit_explain() does
for its SDs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve an enum given as its whole default set
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() resolved an enum setting such as sd_meaning to its
first string only when it was missing. One given as the whole set, as a
wrapper forwarding its own default does, passed arg_match_in_export()
but was recorded as the set in the "scrutiny" attribute, so
grimmer_map_seq() and debit_map_seq() then failed in sd_min_n().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test grouped data in the total-n mappers, reserve the constant column
recent_commits.body:
* The total-n factory picked the reported columns with dplyr::select(),
which adds the grouping columns of a grouped tibble back in, so the
column count no longer matched the pairs and the proto function failed
with a conversion error. The basic and seq tiers were fine with grouped
input. It subsets with `[` now.

* A `constant` column of `data` silently overwrote the values of the
`constant` argument. It is an error now, like the other result columns,
but only if the argument is given.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the value set in the size error, test the limit at its boundary
recent_commits.body:
* check_values_size() now names x, sd, and n of the value set that is
too large; in a vectorized call, nothing said which one it was.

* A test sets VALUES_MAX to the exact number of rows for n = 30, 4, 3,
and 2 and for grim_values(): each passes at the limit and errors one
below it.

* The n = 100 cap case is compared pair by pair with its independent
enumeration, not only by count.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep the rules for three and four numbers in one place
recent_commits.body:
* sum_squares_attainable() scanned for its first sum of squares with
the rules for n = 3 and 4 written out a second time. It now takes the
first window of sum_squares_attainable_all(), which no longer assumes
that `first` is attainable itself, and whose windows start at 8 and
double up to the chunk size, so that the usual early hit stays cheap.
is_loeschian() moves to the test helpers, its only remaining user.

* loeschian_between() clamps by subassignment instead of pmax() and
tabulates instead of sort(), which cost some 20 and 20 microseconds on
the few numbers of a window: 45 microseconds per call before, 10 now.
grimmer() at n = 3 and 4 is still about 10% slower than with the
dedicated scan, on 40,000 value sets taken from samples.

* The test of sum_squares_attainable_all() was circular now that one
calls the other, so it is checked against every sample of up to four
numbers from -6 to 6 instead, from every start. An empty range returned
NULL rather than numeric(0).
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check the grimmer_values() cap cases against independent counts
recent_commits.body:
* The 199,990 pairs at x = 50, sd = 20, n = 100 were only the
implementation's own count. The test now derives them in whole numbers
from the rounding bounds alone, sharing no code with the package.

* The n = 2 case only had to stay below 1e5 rows. It is now compared pair
by pair with an enumeration of two totals by their sum and difference:
14,271 pairs, each with the sum of squares (s^2 + d^2) / 2.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cap the number of means that grim_values() returns
recent_commits.body:
* grim_values() had no limit: n = 1e8 with digits_x = 0 built 2 GB, and
a typo of one more digit would end the session. Like grimmer_values(),
it now errors above a million values per value set, before allocating
them. grim_closest() needs no cap and has none.

* The GRIM vignette shows how to join the output back onto the data by
case, now that the list-column example is gone.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count grimmer_values() pairs exactly, in linear time for n < 5
recent_commits.body:
* For n < 5, each sum's sums of squares were appended with c(), the
quadratic pattern ff3c9d8 removed one level up: 18.6 s for 752k rows at
n = 4, items_averaged = 15. sum_squares_attainable_all() now finds them
in chunks, with a vectorized is_sum_three_squares() for n = 4 and
loeschian_between() for n = 3, which generates the numbers as
x^2 + xy + y^2 rather than testing each with a scan of sqrt(m). That
call takes 0.2 s now, and 286k rows at n = 3 take 0.15 s instead of 19 s.

* The cap of 2694a56 counted every second sum of squares, an upper
bound that is far too high for n = 2, whose sums of squares are sparse:
x = 50, sd = 20, n = 2, items_averaged = 100 was refused as "up to
40,200,101 pairs" and has 14,271. The pairs are now counted as they are
found, and enumeration for n < 5 stops one past the limit.

* check_values_size() and VALUES_MAX hold the limit for both *_values()
functions. The message names items_averaged and sd along with n, which
drive the count as much, and ?grimmer_values states the limit.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

**Text, section, table and statistic extraction from academic papers (PDF, DOCX, HTML), built
for meta-science.**

docpluck turns a research article into text you can run statistical checks on. It extracts the
text layer, repairs the damage extraction itself causes (lost minus signs, split ligatures,
interleaved columns, Greek letters decoded as Latin), identifies the paper's sections, pulls
tables out as cell grids, flattens table rows into records a statistics checker can read, and
renders the whole paper as Markdown. Every output carries a record of what the library had to
guess or refused

recent_commits.body:
Batch of fixes from a two-model check of 10 never-processed psychology papers and
from defects reported by downstream consumers. See CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

Normalization
- extract_pdf runs one pdftotext -bbox pass (restore_line_end_hyphens=True) so
  plain-text callers get the layout-gated hyphen restores; a failed pass is
  recorded as line_end_hyphen_words_unavailable.
- W0v restores a hyphen inside a DOI broken at a line end; W0t handles compounds
  of three or more parts; W0u adjacency fix.
- S6u rejoins a URL or DOI broken across a line; capital-initials and list
  numbers keep the break. A list number is no longer glued onto the previous DOI.
- S0h keeps hyphens in documents whose font encodes the printed hyphen as U+00AD
  (document-level gate).
- P0t strips running titles repeated on later pages, publisher watermark
  sentences and "Downloaded from" stamps; ORCID URLs and supplementary-material
  body lines are kept.

Tables
- fields_raw on every flattened record (printed tokens).
- Typed descriptive pairs (M (SD), b (SE), n (%), est [CI]) with fields["group"]
  per arm column; new keys SE, count, pct.
- Nested spanning headers are not read as arm groups.
- Caption, label and running-head rows leave the grid for the caption; text-only
  tables keep their data rows out of the header.
- A captionless page directly continuing the previous table is linked
  (continuation_of, caption_status "continuation").

Sections and references
- Reference numbers separated from their entries are paired back via layout.
- Group, bare-surname and full-first-name authors start their own entry.
- A wrapped "Supplemental Materials." no longer opens a false section; an
  unheaded abstract of 1200-1500 characters is kept.

Tests: 4309 passed. Snapshot checksums re-pinned for 11 fixtures after verifying
every changed line is a hyphen insertion. 125-paper render diff reviewed: no
statistic lost.

highlights.body: Each table of a file with several has its columns under source_file = "file.xlsx [sheet]", and a new column sheet names the sheet; a file with one table keeps its own name. FAIR_repo() names each variable's CSV by its sheet, writes a CSV per sheet of an .ods file, and writes dataset_description.json also when the first sheet's CSV went to documentation/.

highlights.message: FAIR_repo() works on a temporary copy and keeps recovered code; data_check is faster on large files (#554); code_check no longer writes into your folder
highlights.body:
FAIR_repo() runs its checks on a temporary copy, so the folder is only read. It keeps code recovered from output files as scripts, changes the paths scripts write to, replaces setwd() only for a written-out folder, no folder or the script's own folder, changes links in the folder's README to the files' new places, names each variable's file as it is in the copy, and has an execute argument for the library() calls reproducibility_check adds.

data_check's column checks work on each distinct value once and skip text work for plain number columns; 498 columns compared gave identical results. codebook_check no longer converts columns without documented codes. Pages made by pkgdown are not taken for rendered analyses.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: FAIR_repo() keeps folders, the authors' README and results apart; requirements.txt lists only installable Python packages; output readers keep backslashes
highlights.body:
From converting 20 real repositories:
- psychds_file_plan() keeps a file's folders inside data/, materials/ and
  documentation/ as well as analysis/, ignores a top folder that holds
  every file (GitHub downloads), and drops a first folder that only names
  the kind of file. Data in one folder per condition lost which condition
  it was, and the authors' README was moved out of the top.
- FAIR_repo() puts a file a script writes and no script reads, and a
  fitted model, in outputs/, and points scripts there; converts an R data
  file only when it holds a table and no CSV of that name is next to it;
  writes requirements.txt with Python packages only, without the standard
  library and under their pip names; takes the title from the folder's own
  README; marks missing authors "unknown"; shows variable tables only when
  there are labels; writes no dataset_description.json without data.
- The R, Mplus and Stata output readers pad lines in characters instead of
  with formatC(), which dropped a backslash and split columns wrongly.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Scripts keep their folders inside analysis/
highlights.body:
psychds_file_plan() put every script flat in analysis/, so two scripts
with one name collided and code that finds its own modules by folder
stopped working. A script now keeps its folders below the folder all
scripts of its study share.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: FAIR_repo() converts a local folder and never goes online; identical files are left out; READMEs in subfolders keep their folder; archives of your own are not unpacked into your folder
highlights.body:
FAIR_repo(path, output_dir, paper) now converts a folder on the
researcher's own computer, running the checks as report_repository()
does, with local_only for every check. Nothing is downloaded, no link is
followed, and the folder is not changed. The paper is optional and gives
the title, authors, CRediT roles and funding. Online sources, result
reuse and the download arguments are removed.

A file from an archive that is identical to a file next to it, and a
README identical to another, are left out and listed in CHANGES.md. A data
file that holds no table is kept as it is instead of reported as failed,
and two different originals with one name no longer overwrite each other.
Paths of the folder are removed from the saved check results.

psychds_file_plan() puts a README in a subfolder in documentation/, named
after its folder; every README went to the top and they replaced each
other. .archive_dest() unpacks next to itself only an archive metacheck
downloaded; any archive in the temporary folder counted, so an uploaded
folder got a "<zip>.contents" folder written into it.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: FAIR_repo() writes a reorganised, documented copy of a paper's repository; reproducibility_check copies same-named files from their own place and changes only quoted paths
highlights.body:
FAIR_repo() places every file where the Psych-DS layout puts it, writes
non-CSV data as CSV next to the original, changes the paths and setwd()
lines of R and Python scripts, and writes dataset_description.json,
ro-crate-metadata.json, a README (only where the repository has none),
requirements.txt, CHANGES.md and logs/. It reuses the checks in a captured
result and runs only the missing ones.

reproducibility_check looked up a file's copy by name and took the first,
so same-named files from different folders got one file's content, and it
replaced a path wherever its text appeared, so x.csv also changed
"old_x.csv".

highlights.message: Compare x to a power of 10 in the 15-digit check
highlights.body:
* `abs(x) >= 10^(15 - digits)` is the same condition as the one on
`floor(log10(abs(x)))`, but exact for every power of ten, so it needs
no correction for `log10()` rounding up just below one. The count in
the message comes from the integer part written out.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Show the reported values in full in the size error
highlights.body:
* `check_values_size()` formatted the value set with `format()`'s
default 7 significant digits, so a reported `x = 0.123456789` was
named as `x = 0.1234568`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: ResearchBox read through its API: details, licence, file lists, search and checked downloads
highlights.body:
- rbox_info(), rbox_files(), rbox_search() and rbox_file_download() use
  ResearchBox's API when RESEARCHBOX_API_KEY (or rbox_token()) is set; the
  web page stays the fallback
- downloads are checked against the MD5s in the zip's table of contents (one
  request per box); the table of contents is not listed as a box file
- licence (SPDX id), licence link, public-since and last-modified dates;
  repo_check gives each box's licence in repo_metadata
- peer-review passcodes sent to the API; links to one box merged so a box is
  downloaded once
- requests 6 s apart, Retry-After read, long waits reported
- guard against ResearchBox's 10-day block for non-public boxes; web page
  tells a missing box from one that is not public

highlights.message: Leave one or two missing strings undecided in is_seq_linear()
highlights.body:
* A logical or numeric `NA` is some number, and any two numbers are
linear, but a missing string could be no number at all, so
`is_seq_linear(c(NA_character_, NA_character_))` is `NA` again.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Check an enum in the total-n mappers before n_min_fn() reads it
highlights.body:
* `n_min_fn()` ran on the raw settings, so a two-value or `NULL`
`sd_meaning` failed in `sd_min_n()` with a plain R error instead of
the mapper's own. Each enum given is now validated with
`arg_match_in_export()` right after `resolve_enums()`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Count the integer digits of x exactly in the 15-digit check
highlights.body:
* `floor(log10(abs(x)))` rounds up to the next whole number just below a
power of 10, so 999999999999999 and 99999.9999999999 were rejected as
having 16 significant digits. The exponent is now corrected downward
when `10^exponent` exceeds `abs(x)`, as in `next_square_root()`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject a value with more than 15 significant digits
highlights.body:
* check_newly_numeric() capped digits_x at 15 but not the integer
digits of x, so 33.33333333333333 with digits_x = 14 passed although a
double does not hold 16 significant digits and the tests are not exact
there. The sum of the two is now capped at 15.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Return TRUE for two values with an infinity among them
highlights.body:
* is_seq_linear(c(1, Inf)) was FALSE: the step Inf - 1 is Inf, which
dplyr::near() cannot compare to itself. Any two values are linear, so
the step check only runs for three or more.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Resolve a NULL n_min to the default in every total-n mapper
highlights.body:
* Only the function-valued .n_min branch replaced a NULL, so
grim_map_total_n(n_min = NULL) passed it on to disperse_total(), which
dispersed down to a group of 0.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Report a missing required argument on a 0-row data frame, too
highlights.body:
* A mapper tests its first row on its own so that a missing digits_x or
items_averaged is reported by the test function. With no row to test,
the check was skipped and the mapper returned an empty tibble. It now
tests a row of missing values if a required argument is missing.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung
